paragraph: Angola's payments law is [Lei n.º 40/20 of 16 December 2020, the Lei do Sistema de Pagamentos de Angola](<https://lex.ao/docs/banco-nacional-de-angola/2022/aviso-n-o-2-22-de-02-de-fevereiro/>). Under it, [Aviso n.º 2/22 of February 2022](<https://lex.ao/docs/banco-nacional-de-angola/2022/aviso-n-o-2-22-de-02-de-fevereiro/>) lets non-bank financial institutions provide payment services as authorised payment service companies. In the last twelve months, [Aviso n.º 1/26 of January 2026](<https://lex.ao/docs/banco-nacional-de-angola/2026/aviso-n-o-1-26-de-28-de-janeiro/>) set the rules for acquirers that are not banks, and only authorised companies may now act as non-bank acquirers. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Burundi's [Loi n°1/07 of 11 May 2018 on the national payment system](<https://www.brb.bi/sites/default/files/2024-09/LOI%20N%201-07%20DU%2011%20MAI%202018%20PORTANT%20SYSTEME%20NATIONAL%20DE%20PAIMENT.pdf>) is in force, and the central bank's oversight framework of November 2025 [cites it as the current law](<https://www.brb.bi/sites/default/files/2025-11/CADRE%20DE%20SURVEILLANCE%20DE%20SYSTEME%20DE%20PAIEMENT%20%2020%20NOV%202025.pdf>). Under it the bank made [Règlement n°002/2024](<https://www.brb.bi/sites/default/files/2025-11/CADRE%20DE%20SURVEILLANCE%20DE%20SYSTEME%20DE%20PAIEMENT%20%2020%20NOV%202025.pdf>), which revises a 2017 regulation and under which it licenses payment institutions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Benin is bound by the BCEAO's [Instruction n°001-01-2024 on payment services](<https://techcabal.com/2026/02/17/francophone-weekly-by-techcabal-012/>), applied since January 2024. It requires every company offering payment services in the union to hold a licence or stop. [Four companies held payment institution licences in Benin](<https://beninwebtv.bj/benin-quatre-etablissements-paiement-agrees-aout-2026/>) at 31 August 2026. In the last twelve months, the BCEAO told banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions to connect to its instant payment platform, PI-SPI. On 25 June 2026 it [moved the deadline to 30 September](<https://www.bceao.int/sites/default/files/2026-06/Communiqu%C3%A9_Prolongation_d%C3%A9lai_Connexion_%C3%A0_PI-SPI-25062026.pdf>). Since 2 November 2026 a BCEAO notice [requires interoperable e-money transfers to go through PI-SPI](<https://triomphemag.com/interoperabilite-du-mobile-money-au-benin-pi-spi-entre-en-vigueur-ce-qui-change-reellement-pour-les-utilisateurs-des-ce-2-novembre/>).

Burkina Faso is bound by the BCEAO's [instruction of 23 January 2024 on payment services](<https://beninwebtv.bj/benin-quatre-etablissements-paiement-agrees-aout-2026/>), under which payment institutions are licensed. [Two payment institutions are licensed in Burkina Faso](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees-dans-lumoa-au-31-aout-2026>). INTOUCH Burkina has held a licence since 9 May 2025 and KERRY Payments Burkina since 2 September 2025. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, the BCEAO told every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution to connect to its instant payment platform, PI-SPI, by 30 June. On 25 June it [moved the deadline to 30 September 2026](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-finance/0110-142036-wave-rejoint-la-plateforme-de-paiement-instantane-de-la-bceao-un-an-apres-son-lancement>). L'Oeil du Sahel reports [a BCEAO communique of 2 October 2026 requiring interoperable e-money transfers to pass through PI-SPI from 2 November 2026](<https://oeildusahel.com/pi-spi-mobile-money-impact-economique-aes/>).

Botswana's [Electronic Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations, 2026](<https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/sites/default/files/Electronic%20Payment%20Services%20(Amendment)%20Regulations%2C%202026.pdf>), made by the Minister of Finance as Statutory Instrument No. 46 of 2026, [took effect on 2 April 2026](<https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/sites/default/files/press-release-files/Implementation%20of%20the%20Electronic%20Payment%20Services%20%28Amendment%29%20Regulations%2C%202026.pdf>). In the last twelve months, they began to require anyone operating an electronic payment service, e-money issuance included, to hold a Bank of Botswana licence and be a company incorporated in Botswana. They do not apply to banks licensed under the Banking Act. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

The Central African Republic is bound by [CEMAC regulation n°04/18 of 21 December 2018 on payment services](<https://www.beac.int/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Strat%C3%A9gie-R%C3%A9gionale-dInclusion-Financi%C3%A8re-de-la-CEMAC.pdf>). The regional central bank's strategy of February 2025 says the regulation created payment establishments, licensed to provide payment services without being tied to a bank. The strategy lists six licensed across the region by July 2023, and none was in the Central African Republic. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Côte d'Ivoire is bound by the BCEAO's [Instruction n°001-01-2024 on payment services, applied since January 2024](<https://techcabal.com/2026/02/17/francophone-weekly-by-techcabal-012/>). [Ten payment institutions were licensed in Côte d'Ivoire at 31 August 2026](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees-dans-lumoa-au-31-aout-2026>), the newest on 27 April 2026. In the last twelve months, [in April 2026 the BCEAO told every bank and e-money and payment institution to connect to PI-SPI by 30 June](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2641755/economie/uemoa-linteroperabilite-des-paiements-devient-obligatoire-des-le-30-juin-2026>). [On 25 June it moved the deadline to 30 September 2026](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-finance/0110-142036-wave-rejoint-la-plateforme-de-paiement-instantane-de-la-bceao-un-an-apres-son-lancement>). [On 4 November 2026 a National Assembly committee adopted a 258-article banking bill](<https://www.linfodrome.com/economie/127262-banques-fintech-monnaie-electronique-la-cote-d-ivoire-prepare-une-nouvelle-reglementation>). The bill brings fintech and e-money operations into national law.

[Cameroon's regulatory framework](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-finance/1709-141667-cameroun-konoom-obtient-son-agrement-et-se-lance-sur-le-marche-du-paiement-mobile>) lets payment institutions, banks and microfinance institutions offer payment services, with a licence granted by order of the finance minister on a decision of COBAC, the regional banking commission. In the last twelve months, [Konoom Cameroun was licensed as a payment institution](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-finance/1709-141667-cameroun-konoom-obtient-son-agrement-et-se-lance-sur-le-marche-du-paiement-mobile>) by arrêté n°681/MINFI of 21 July 2026. Orange Money Cameroun and Mobile Money Corporation were already licensed. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

[Loi n° 18-019 of 9 July 2018](<https://anapi.cd/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/221.07.18-Loi-du-9-juillet-2018_Systemes-de-paiement-1.pdf>) on payment systems is the Democratic Republic of the Congo's payments law. [The central bank's map of the payment system lists the providers it has approved](<https://www.bcc.cd/intermediaires-financiers/systemes-de-paiement/infrastructures>), five non-bank financial companies among them at end-2023. [Instruction No. 58 of September 2024](<https://regalert.today/document/instruction-no-58-on-the-interoperability-of-electronic-payment-systems-and-part-34b2c78f-c351-4d8d-a6ee-2eba0ba23e98>) obliges every regulated entity to join the National E-Payment Switch within six months, under sanction. In the last twelve months, the central bank [licensed Wave as an e-money institution in November 2026](<https://leconomie.info/article/rdc-wave-decroche-le-feu-vert-reglementaire-de-la-banque-centrale-pour-lancer-ses-operations>).

Congo's payment institutions are governed by [CEMAC/UMAC/COBAC Regulation No. 04/18 of 21 December 2018 on payment services](<https://www.sgg.cg/textes-officiels/arretes/2025/congo-arrete-2025-1672.pdf>). The finance ministry [approved Mobile Money Congo SA as a payment institution by an order of 27 May 2022](<https://www.sgg.cg/textes-officiels/arretes/2025/congo-arrete-2025-1672.pdf>). In the last twelve months, COBAC's [2025 annual report](<https://ecomatin.net/cemac-le-mobile-money-brasse-44-000-milliards-fcfa-en-2025-et-genere-47-milliards-de-benefices-aux-operateurs>) named Mobile Money Congo SA and Mobile Commerce Congo SA as the payment institutions operating in Congo, neither a bank. Their revenues rose 28.1% to FCFA 20.6 billion in 2025. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

The Central Bank of the Comoros issued [Regulation n°01/2017/BCC/DSBR](<https://banque-comores.km/uploads/Loi%20et%20textes%20reglementaire/REGLEMENTS/2017/R%C3%A8glement%20n%C2%B001_2017_BCC_DSBR%20sur%20la%20monnaie%20%C3%A9lectronique.pdf>) in 2017, setting the conditions for carrying on e-money activity. No later amendment is reported. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, [the central bank listed Telco Money SA and Hury Money SA among the e-money institutions legally established in the Comoros](<https://finances.gouv.km/actualite_post/communique-de-la-banque-centrale-des-comores-sur-lexercice-illegal-dactivites-bancaires-offshores/>), beside its licensed banks. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Cabo Verde legislated on payments in three decree-laws published on 28 November 2018. [Decreto-legislativo n.º 7/2018](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/Download/2610>) sets the regime for the payment system, and [Decreto-legislativo n.º 8/2018](<https://www.bcv.cv/pt/SistemadePagamentos/Paginas/SistemadePagamentos.aspx>) regulates payment services and e-money. Under [Decreto-legislativo n.º 9/2018](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/Download/2610>), the Banco de Cabo Verde authorises payment institutions and e-money institutions, which are distinct from banks. No licensed institution has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Djibouti's [Loi n° 118/AN/15/7ème L](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/loi-n118-an-15-7eme-l-portant-creation-dun-systeme-de-paiement-national-sa-reglementation-et-sa-surveillance/>), which created the National Payment System, was promulgated in 2016 and applies to every payment service and system. The central bank's [register of licensed institutions](<https://banque-centrale.dj/les-etablissements-agrees/>) lists two e-money issuers beside the banks, D-Money (licensed 2020) and WAAFI (licensed 2022). No amendment to the law has been found, and no change in the last twelve months. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Algeria's [Loi n° 23-09 of 21 June 2023 on money and banking](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-FRANCAIS/2023/F2023043.pdf>) lists payment service providers apart from banks. Under it the Bank of Algeria made [Regulation no. 25-02 of 14 April 2025](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-FRANCAIS/2025/F2025028.pdf>), which lets a company be licensed as one by the Governor after authorisation by the Monetary and Banking Council. In the last twelve months, on 23 September 2026 the Council [authorised Djezzy Payment Services](<https://www.bank-of-algeria.dz/stoodroa/2026/09/communique-23-09-2026FR.pdf>), a subsidiary of a mobile operator, to set itself up as a provider. It has twelve months to apply for the licence. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

The Central Bank of Egypt issued [Rules for Licensing and Registration of Payment System Operators and Payment Service Providers](<https://www.cbe.org.eg/en/news-publications/news/2025/09/01/13/10/payment-system-operators-and-payment-service-providers>) in June 2025. The [rules of 19 June 2025](<https://www.cbe.org.eg/en/news-publications/news/2025/06/19/08/20/psos-and-psps-licensing-rules>) set licensing conditions, minimum capital and financial guarantees for payment institutions, and existing ones had twelve months to apply for a licence. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

The National Bank of Ethiopia introduced [two sets of rules in 2020](<https://www.thereporterethiopia.com/52044/>): the Payment Instrument Issuers directives and the Payment Systems Operators directive. Companies that are not banks, among them Chapa, Arifpay, Santimpay and Kacha, were licensed under the operators directive. [Directive ONPS/10/2025 entered into force on 12 May 2025](<https://nbe.gov.et/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/ONPS102025-Oversight-of-the-Natioanl-Payment-System-Licensing-and-Authorization-of-Payment-Instrument-Issuer-Amendment-Directive.pdf>). It requires issuers to make their wallets interoperate through the national switch or another licensed switch. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No act of parliament on payments is named.

Gabon is bound by [CEMAC regulation n°04/18 of 21 December 2018 on payment services](<https://droitmediasfinance.com/index.php/actualites/droit-tech-fintech/1262-cemac-transferts-de-fonds-via-les-fintechs-une-nouvelle-instruction-beac-precise-les-diligences-relatives-au-traitement-et-suivi-des-prefinancements-des-operations-de-remittance-entrante-executees-par-le-canal-des-etablissements-de-paiement>), which a BEAC instruction of 5 May 2026 supplements. In the last twelve months, the Council of Ministers [adopted a draft ordinance on digital payments](<https://gouvernement.ga/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Communique-final-publiee-du-Conseil-du-29-janvier-2026-1.pdf>) on 29 January 2026, and on 22 May the digital economy minister [defended the bill ratifying it](<https://www.focusgroupemedia.com/gabon-modernisation-de-letat-le-cadre-juridique-des-paiements-digitaux-en-examen-a-lassemblee-nationale/>) before the National Assembly's finance committee. COBAC's 2025 report [names Airtel Money Gabon and Clikpay Gabon](<https://ecomatin.net/cemac-le-mobile-money-brasse-44-000-milliards-fcfa-en-2025-et-genere-47-milliards-de-benefices-aux-operateurs>) as payment institutions. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other. Mature would need such a rule.

Ghana's [Payment Systems and Services Act, 2019 (Act 987)](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-ghana>) has applied since February 2020. It requires payment service providers and e-money issuers to hold a Bank of Ghana licence. Ghana [mandated mobile money interoperability in 2018](<https://iafrikan.com/tomorrow-west-africas-central-bank-finds-out-who-really-runs-its-payments-market>), and the rule that did so is not named. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the Bank [listed 63 approved non-bank entities](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/FinTech-Sector-Report-2026-Q1-2.pdf>). On 14 July 2026 it [revoked a licence under section 13](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/bog-officials-police-restrict-access-to-zeepay-headquarters-after-licence-revocation/>). It was the dedicated e-money issuer licence of Zeepay Ghana, withdrawn over inadequate cash backing of its e-money.

The central bank's licensing committee issued [Decision D/2015/003/CAM on 31 March 2015](<https://www.bcrg-guinee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Recueil-des-textes-legaux-et-reglementaires-regissant-lactivite-bancaire-et-financiere-%E2%80%93-Dec-201.pdf>), which governs e-money and the firms that issue it. It classes them as financial establishments, not banks, and [requires each to hold a central bank licence](<https://www.bcrg-guinee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Recueil-des-textes-legaux-et-reglementaires-regissant-lactivite-bancaire-et-financiere-%E2%80%93-Dec-201.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the central bank was [preparing a bill on payment systems and instruments](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites/2610-142742-guinee-nimbapay-traite-7-6-millions-de-transactions-et-connecte-7-etablissements-en-4-mois>), with no text published. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

The Gambia's central bank made the [Mobile Money Regulation, 2011](<https://www.cbg.gm/downloads-file/b2064e61-f37b-11e9-876c-02e599c15748>), which took effect on 15 October 2011. [It provides for retail transfers by persons not licensed as banks](<https://www.cbg.gm/downloads-file/b2064e61-f37b-11e9-876c-02e599c15748>) and has the central bank authorise such providers as limited liability companies. The [Electronic Payments System Act 2013](<https://www.cbg.gm/downloads-file/448bc45a-06e7-11ea-876c-02e599c15748>) defines the establishment and operation of the electronic payments system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Guinea-Bissau is bound by the BCEAO's [Instruction n°001-01-2024 on payment services](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees-dans-lumoa-au-31-aout-2026>), under which payment institutions are licensed. The banking commission's register [lists one payment institution and one e-money institution in Guinea-Bissau](<https://www.bceao.int/sites/default/files/inline-files/4%20-%20Liste%20Guin%C3%A9e-Bissau_2026.pdf>). They are INTOUCH Guinée-Bissau and Finances Mobiles Bissau. In the last twelve months, the BCEAO required every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution to connect to its instant payment platform, PI-SPI, by 30 June 2026. On 25 June it [moved the deadline to 30 September](<https://financesao.com/uemoa-pi-spi-atteint-104-etablissements-autorises/>). Five institutions in Guinea-Bissau were authorised on the platform at 31 July 2026.

Equatorial Guinea is bound by [CEMAC regulation n°04/18 of 21 December 2018 on payment services](<https://www.beac.int/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Strat%C3%A9gie-R%C3%A9gionale-dInclusion-Financi%C3%A8re-de-la-CEMAC.pdf>). The regional central bank's strategy of February 2025 says the regulation created payment establishments, licensed to provide payment services without being tied to a bank. The strategy lists six licensed across the region by July 2023, and none was in Equatorial Guinea. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Kenya's [National Payment System Act 2011](<https://www.centralbank.go.ke/national-payments-system/>) is the legal framework for payment systems and providers, with the National Payment System Regulations 2014 under it. [Mobile phone money transfer operators are authorised as payment service providers](<https://www.centralbank.go.ke/national-payments-system/>) under them. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the National Treasury and the Central Bank of Kenya [published a draft National Payment System Bill, 2026](<https://www.centralbank.go.ke/2026/09/21/draft-national-payment-system-policy-and-national-payment-system-bill-2026/>) to repeal and replace the Act, with comments due by 9 October. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

The Central Bank of Liberia's [Mobile Money Regulations](<https://www.cbl.org.lr/sites/default/files/documents/MobileMoneyRegulations.pdf>) are the framework governing e-money and mobile money operators, and the bank is the regulator. In June 2024 it [fined Lonestar Cell MTN Mobile Money Inc. for persistent breaches of its mobile money regulations](<https://www.micat.gov.lr/media/lina-daily-news-bulletin/monrovia-june-15-lina-lonestar-cell-mtn-mobile-money-inc-prominent>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found that says the regulations license companies that are not banks, or names one licensed under them. Operating would need a source that says companies that are not banks can be licensed under the rules in force, or names one licensed.

Libya's [Law No. 6 of 2022 on Electronic Transactions](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-6-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2022-%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%B4%D8%A3%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%85%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%84%D9%83/>) defines e-money. The Central Bank's [circular 18 of 2025](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B4%D9%88%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-18-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2025-%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%B4%D8%A3%D9%86-%D9%86%D8%B8%D8%A7%D9%85-%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D9%8A/>) is addressed to the electronic payment companies it has licensed, which are not banks. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 [the Central Bank agreed that the IMF will help its teams draft an updated licensing regulation for electronic payment companies](<https://www.cbl.gov.ly/en/governor-of-the-central-bank-of-libya-discusses-with-the-international-monetary-fund-strengthening-the-legal-frameworks-for-financial-governance-and-combating-financial-crimes/>). No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Lesotho's [Payment Systems Act, 2014](<https://centralbank.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/Payment-Systems-Act-2014-1.pdf>) was published in the Government Gazette on 12 September 2014 and came into operation that day. In the last twelve months, on 5 May 2026 the Minister of Finance [moved the Payment System Bill, 2025 for second reading](<https://www.lena.gov.ls/finance-minister-presents-payment-system-bill/>) in the National Assembly. The bill would repeal the Act and license all payment service providers. It had [first been presented on 2 May 2025](<https://nationalassembly.parliament.ls/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Report-Payment-Systems-Bill-2025.pdf>). No source has been found that says companies that are not banks can be licensed under the Act in force. Operating would need a source that says so, or names one licensed.

Morocco's [Law 103-12 on credit institutions](<https://www.bkam.ma/content/download/757666/8545663/loi%20bancaire%20fr%2022.pdf>), enacted on 24 December 2014, defines payment institutions as entities separate from credit institutions, which need Bank Al-Maghrib's approval before operating. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 Bank Al-Maghrib and the Competition Council said that [newly licensed payment institutions](<https://conseil-concurrence.ma/communique-conjoint-du-conseil-de-la-concurrence-et-de-bank-al-maghrib/>) and older ones were taking up card acquiring. [Switch Al Maghrib says newly licensed payment institutions joined its mobile payment hub](<https://www.swam.ma/>). No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Madagascar's [Loi n°2016-056 on electronic money and electronic money institutions](<https://textes.lexxika.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Loi-2016-056-02-Fevrier-2016-Sur-la-Monnaie-Electronique-et-les-Etablissements-de-Monnaie-Electronique.pdf>) was promulgated on 2 February 2017. [It requires any legal entity running e-money operations to be approved by the CSBF](<https://textes.lexxika.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Loi-2016-056-02-Fevrier-2016-Sur-la-Monnaie-Electronique-et-les-Etablissements-de-Monnaie-Electronique.pdf>) as an e-money institution. Such an institution is separate from credit institutions. In October 2024 the central bank [made connection to its instant payment system compulsory](<https://2424.mg/adhesion-obligatoire-au-systeme-de-paiement-instantane-de-la-banque-centrale-pour-les-institutions-financieres/>) for banks and e-money institutions, with a deadline of 31 January 2025. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 the central bank governor [announced audits of the e-money institutions](<https://2424.mg/mobile-money-les-autorites-annoncent-des-audits-du-systeme-des-etablissements-de-monnaie-electronique/>).

Mali is bound by the BCEAO's [Instruction n°001-01-2024 on payment services](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees-dans-lumoa-au-31-aout-2026>), under which payment institutions are licensed. [Two payment institutions are licensed in Mali](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees-dans-lumoa-au-31-aout-2026>): INTOUCH Mali, since 9 May 2025, and CAURIDOR, since 3 September 2025. In April 2026 the BCEAO told every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution to connect to PI-SPI by 30 June. In the last twelve months, on 25 June it [set 30 September 2026 as the new deadline](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/prolongation-du-delai-de-connexion-a-pi-spi>). L'Oeil du Sahel reports [a BCEAO communique of 2 October 2026 requiring interoperable e-money transfers to pass through PI-SPI from 2 November 2026](<https://oeildusahel.com/pi-spi-mobile-money-impact-economique-aes/>).

Mozambique's [Lei n.º 15/2026 of 2 July](<https://www.bancomoc.mz/pt/media/noticias/lei-n-%C2%BA-15-2026-de-2-de-julho-aprova-a-lei-do-sistema-nacional-de-pagamentos/>) approves the National Payments System Law and revokes Lei n.º 2/2008. Parliament [approved it in April](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/mozambique-national-payments-system-law-unanimously-approved-by-parliament/>) and the president promulgated it in June. In the last twelve months, that law replaced the 2008 law. Three electronic money institutions [authorised by the central bank](<https://360mozambique.com/economy/banking/metix-instant-payment-system-surpasses-11000-daily-transfers/>), M-Pesa, e-Mola and M-Kesh, belong to the three mobile operators. [Article 8 of the regulation annexed to Aviso n.º 1/GBM/2026](<https://www.bancomoc.mz/media/1bwihts1/aviso-1-gbm-2026.pdf>) makes participation in the instant payment system compulsory for them and for credit institutions above a set size.

Mauritania's [Loi n°2021-014 of 5 July 2021](<https://www.droit-afrique.com/uploads/Mauritanie-Loi-2021-14-services-moyens-paiement-electronique.pdf>) on electronic payment services regulates payment service providers and e-money issuers, and bars anyone except banks from running a payment institution or issuing e-money without the central bank's licence. The central bank issued [Instruction no. 03/GR/2022 of 31 March 2022](<https://fintech.bcm.mr/download/instruction_03_gr_2022-2%20Portant%20reglementation%20des%20%C3%A9tablissements%20de%20paiement.pdf>) regulating payment institutions. In the last twelve months, [in November 2026 Le Quotidien reported that Mattel Money, a mobile operator's subsidiary, is licensed by the central bank as an e-money institution](<https://lequotidien.mr/?p=42746>). No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other. Mature would need such a rule.

Mauritius's [National Payment Systems Act 2018](<https://mauritiusassembly.govmu.org/mauritiusassembly/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/act1718.pdf>) was assented to on 29 November 2018 and makes the Bank of Mauritius the regulator of payment service providers. In the last twelve months, the Act was [last amended in April 2026](<https://mauritiusassembly.govmu.org/mauritiusassembly/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Act0326.pdf>), and the Bank's [Guideline for Payment Aggregators](<https://www.bom.mu/sites/default/files/guideline_for_payment_aggregators_0.pdf>) took effect on 31 August 2026. It requires non-bank companies acting as payment aggregators to hold a licence. [The Bank's list of licensees](<https://www.bom.mu/payment-systems/licensing/list-licensees>) names Emtel MFS Co Ltd, Cellplus Mobile Communications Limited and EZ Dash Limited. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other. Mature would need such a rule.

On 30 September 2026 the Reserve Bank of Malawi [issued a payment service provider licence](<https://malawi24.com/2026/10/17/payment-hurdles-ease-for-businesses/>) to PayChangu Limited under the Payment Systems Act, 2016. The company is a local fintech and not a bank. In the last twelve months, on 6 August 2026 [Parliament passed an amendment to the Act](<https://malawi24.com/2026/08/07/mps-hailed-for-fast-tracking-digital-finance-reforms/>) removing its provisions on cheques. The Finance Minister said detailed regulations would follow. No source has been found that says a rule requires mobile money providers and banks to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Namibia's [Payment System Management Act 14 of 2023](<https://www.bon.com.na/CMSTemplates/Bon/Files/bon.com.na/94/94193758-e15b-4af9-8321-4801142c82f7.pdf>) was promulgated on 28 July 2023 and commenced on 8 August 2023. [PSD-1 on licensing](<https://www.bon.com.na/CMSTemplates/Bon/Files/bon.com.na/31/313b4ab5-b138-45d3-b526-28959686db96.pdf>) took effect on 6 January 2026. It sets a licensing process for payment services by non-bank financial institutions. [Directive PSDIR-11 of 16 June 2025](<https://www.bon.com.na/CMSTemplates/Bon/Files/bon.com.na/57/57989e72-2303-40db-9617-01d97d88abbf.pdf>) requires every provider issuing payment instruments to make e-money interoperable through the instant payment switch by 26 February 2026. In the last twelve months, [PSD-10 on fees and charges](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2025/8816.pdf>) took effect on 24 December 2025. [PSD-12 on operational and cybersecurity standards](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2026/8968.pdf>) took effect on 3 July 2026.

The banking commission of the West African monetary union [counted one licensed e-money issuer in Niger](<https://www.horonyafinance.com/umoa-la-monnaie-electronique-gagne-du-terrain-les-encours-bondissent-de-352-en-2025/>) at 31 December 2025. It is not a bank. Niger follows the BCEAO's rules. In April 2026 the BCEAO [told every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution in the eight states](<https://iafrikan.com/tomorrow-west-africas-central-bank-finds-out-who-really-runs-its-payments-market>) to connect to PI-SPI by 30 June 2026. In the last twelve months, on 25 June it [set 30 September 2026 as the new deadline](<https://financesao.com/uemoa-pi-spi-atteint-104-etablissements-autorises/>). L'Oeil du Sahel reports [a BCEAO communique of 2 October 2026 requiring interoperable e-money transfers to pass through PI-SPI from 2 November 2026](<https://oeildusahel.com/pi-spi-mobile-money-impact-economique-aes/>).

[OPay's October 2026 US filing names the central bank's licensing frameworks](<https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2103076/000119312526418812/d56487df1.htm>) for payment service banks, mobile money operators and payment service providers, which it says opened payments to non-bank players. In the last twelve months those frameworks were cited and not changed: [operators told a March 2026 hearing that the central bank licenses them](<https://businesstech.ng/fintech-regulatory-commission-bill-nigeria/>), mobile money operators and digital banks among them. Payments already clear through NIBSS Instant Payment, but joining it is not shown to be required. No rule has been found that binds providers and banks to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

The National Bank of Rwanda issued [Directive No. 45/2026 on 9 January 2026](<https://rba.rw/a-fully-connected-rwanda-what-ekash-interoperability-means-for-the-future-of-financial-inclusion/>). It [required domestic retail payments between banks and electronic money issuers](<https://itweb.africa/article/rwanda-migrates-retail-payments-to-ekash/rxP3jqBEnOoMA2ye>) to move to the eKash platform, the national instant payment rail. In the last twelve months, [from 14 July 2026 every transfer between bank accounts and electronic money issuers is routed through eKash](<https://itweb.africa/article/rwanda-migrates-retail-payments-to-ekash/rxP3jqBEnOoMA2ye>). This includes account to wallet and wallet to wallet. The Rwanda Bankers' Association states that [the directive took effect on that date](<https://rba.rw/a-fully-connected-rwanda-what-ekash-interoperability-means-for-the-future-of-financial-inclusion/>). The law under which those issuers are licensed is not named.

Sudan's central bank approved its [Regulation on Licensing and Organising Mobile Payment Financial Institutions 2020](<https://cbos.gov.sd/ar/content/%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%AD%D8%A9-%D8%AA%D8%B1%D8%AE%D9%8A%D8%B5-%D9%88%D8%AA%D9%86%D8%B8%D9%8A%D9%85-%D8%A3%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A4%D8%B3%D8%B3%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%84%D9%84%D8%AF%D9%81%D8%B9-%D8%B9%D8%A8%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%8A%D9%84-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2020>) on 28 December 2020. It has the central bank license companies that are not banks to run mobile payment and open e-money wallet accounts. In the last twelve months, [Circular 7/2026 of 31 March 2026](<https://cbos.gov.sd/ar/node/24567/>) set binding minimum rules for financial services over USSD. It asks providers to connect to a national switch once one is available, and sets no date. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Senegal is bound by the BCEAO's [instruction of 23 January 2024 on payment services](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Economie/mobile-money-pourquoi-le-duel-orange-money-wave-ne-resume-plus-le-marche_n_505004.html>), the rule under which payment institutions are licensed. [Eleven payment institutions were licensed in Senegal](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees-dans-lumoa-au-31-aout-2026>) at 31 August 2026, Flutterwave Sénégal and Julaya Sénégal among them. In the last twelve months, by a communiqué of 25 June 2026 the BCEAO [set 30 September 2026 as the deadline](<https://www.bceao.int/sites/default/files/2026-06/Communiqu%C3%A9_Prolongation_d%C3%A9lai_Connexion_%C3%A0_PI-SPI-25062026.pdf>). It applies to banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions connecting to PI-SPI, its instant payment platform. [From 2 November 2026 the BCEAO required interoperable e-money transfers to go through PI-SPI](<https://launchbaseafrica.com/2026/11/03/failed-transfers-hidden-fees-and-phantom-aliases-inside-the-messy-birth-of-west-africas-unified-payments-network/>).

Sierra Leone's [National Payment Systems Act, 2022](<https://sierralii.gov.sl/akn/sl/act/2022/8/eng@2022-06-23>) was assented to on 2 June 2022 and commenced on 23 June 2022, repealing the Payment Systems Act 2009. [Section 6 bars anyone from providing payment services](<https://sierralii.gov.sl/akn/sl/act/2022/8/eng@2022-06-23>) without a Bank of Sierra Leone licence, so the licence is one for companies that are not banks. Directives issued in December 2024 [require all commercial banks and mobile money operators](<https://www.sierraleonemonitor.com/bank-of-sierra-leone-issues-national-payment-switch-directives-for-2024/>) to route payments through the national switch. No change has been found in the last twelve months. In April 2025 the bank [moved the deadline for joining from 31 March to 30 June 2025](<https://apanews.net/bank-of-sierra-leone-extends-national-switch-integration-deadline/>).

The Central Bank of Somalia made the [Mobile Money Regulations, Amended 2020](<https://centralbank.gov.so/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Mobile-Money-Regulation-2020_amended_2021.pdf>) under its 2012 Act. They set out the licensing and supervision of mobile money service providers. A National Payment System Bill [would let the central bank license payment systems and digital money platforms](<https://golekaab.so/en/bill/15>), and the House of the People passed it on 8 November 2025. In the last twelve months, the Upper House [passed its third reading on 11 January 2026](<https://sonna.so/en/somalias-upper-house-passes-national-payment-system-bill-receives-briefing-on-worsening-drought/>), and in October 2026 the House of the People [approved a separate Digital Transactions Bill](<https://www.africa-newsroom.com/press/somalias-house-of-the-people-approves-the-digital-transactions-bill-with-137-votes-in-favour>). Signing of the first bill is not reported. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other. Mature would need such a rule.

South Sudan's [Electronic Money Regulation 2017 Amendment 2025](<https://radioyei.org/news/technology/boss-sets-strict-usd-caps-on-mobile-money/>) took effect, as reported, on 1 September 2026. It was issued under the Bank of South Sudan Act 2011 Amendment 2023. Under it [non-bank e-money issuers are licensed](<https://radioyei.org/news/technology/boss-sets-strict-usd-caps-on-mobile-money/>). Every digital payment platform must connect to the National Payment System through a licensed switch. In the last twelve months, the Bank of South Sudan [opened a five-day workshop on 10 August 2026](<https://www.eyeradio.org/boss-parliament-back-stronger-legal-framework-for-digital-payments/>) to validate the broader National Payment System Bill, 2025, which is still a draft. At its close the governor [called for faster progress](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/17/south-sudan-pushes-digital-payments-as-central-bank-calls-for-faster-payment-bill/>).

São Tomé and Príncipe's [Lei n.º 17/2018](<https://www.africa-laws.org/Saotome/banking%20and%20finance%20law/Law%20no%2017-2018%20%20Legal%20System%20of%20the%20National%20Payment%20System%20(in%20Portuguese).pdf>) was published on 7 September 2018 and sets the legal regime for the National Payment System. It lets the central bank authorise and license payment service providers, e-money issuance included, while banks need no new authorisation. The central bank's organic law, [Lei n.º 03/2025](<https://www.bcstp.st/Upload/Documentos/Gabinete_Governador/Lei_organica.pdf>), makes it responsible for regulating payment systems. No licensed provider has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Eswatini's [National Payments System Act, 2023](<https://www.centralbank.org.sz/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/NATIONAL-PAYMENT-SYSTEM-ACT-2023.pdf>) regulates payment systems and payment service providers. The central bank said in November 2025 that [licensing runs under it now](<https://techcabal.com/2025/11/13/how-a-small-country-is-tackling-big-payments-challenges/>). Fast payments launched on the Eswatini Payment Switch on 11 December 2024. The Governor said [participation is mandated for all payment service providers](<https://www.bis.org/review/r250114f.htm>) offering local payments. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [A central bank directive binds all licensed payment service providers from 31 March 2025](<https://www.centralbank.org.sz/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Eswatini-CMA-Retail-EFT-Payment-Directive-v1.pdf>). It gives them until 31 March 2027 to move low-value transfers within the Common Monetary Area to the TCIB scheme.

Seychelles' [National Payment System Act, 2014](<https://seylii.org/akn/sc/act/2014/14/eng@2014-08-18>) commenced on 18 August 2014. Under it the Central Bank made the [Electronic Money Regulations, 2022](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2023-01/SI%20128%202022%20-%20National%20Payment%20System%20%28Electronic%20Money%29%20Regulations%2C%202022.pdf>), which commenced on 12 December 2022 and set capital and liquidity rules for issuers other than banks. In the last twelve months, on 15 December 2025 it [amended its licensing and authorisation regulations](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2025-12/SI%2099%202025%20No%202%20-%20National%20Payment%20System%20%28Licensing%20and%20Authorisation%29%20%28Amendment%29%20Regulations%202025.pdf>), setting the conditions on which it may license any company incorporated under the Companies Act as a payment service provider. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Chad is bound by [the CEMAC regulation of 21 December 2018 on payment services](<https://leconomie.info/tchad-moov-money-rejoint-le-club-restreint-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees/>), the framework under which its payment establishments are licensed. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 COBAC confirmed [Moov Money Tchad, a telecom subsidiary, as a payment establishment](<https://leconomie.info/tchad-moov-money-rejoint-le-club-restreint-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees/>). It is the third company that is not a bank so licensed in Chad, after Airtel Money in 2023 and Konoom in 2025. In February 2026 the finance ministry [signed conventions with four such operators](<https://tchadinfos.com/2026/02/18/digitalisation-des-paiements-publics-le-ministere-des-finances-signe-des-partenariats-avec-des-operateurs-de-mobile-money/>) on mobile money for state payments. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other. Mature would need such a rule.

A [BCEAO communique of 2 October 2026](<https://www.bceao.int/sites/default/files/2026-10/Communiqu%C3%A9%20du%202%20octobre%202026.pdf>) sets binding terms for e-money transfers between persons through PI-SPI from 2 November. Togo follows the BCEAO's rules. [Tmoney was licensed as an e-money institution in September 2025](<https://cadreco.media/finance/2026/umoa-les-transactions-mobiles-atteignent-164169-milliards-de-francs-cfa-en-2025>). In the last twelve months, on 25 June 2026 the BCEAO [moved the deadline to 30 September](<https://financesao.com/uemoa-pi-spi-atteint-104-etablissements-autorises/>) for banks, e-money issuers and payment institutions to connect to PI-SPI. A [BCEAO instruction of 8 October 2026](<https://www.togofirst.com/en/finance/1210-20312-bceao-to-double-mobile-money-account-limit-to-cfaf-4-million>) raises the e-money balance cap to CFAF 4 million per issuer, from CFAF 2 million since 2015. Since 2 November 2026 [e-money transfers between individuals across providers must go through PI-SPI](<https://togotimes.info/paiements-numeriques-le-togo-accelere-vers-linstantane/>).

Tunisia's [Law n° 2016-48 of 11 July 2016 on banks and financial institutions](<https://www.cmf.tn/sites/default/files/pdfs/reglementation/textes-reference/loi2016_48_fr.pdf>) has payment services run by a specialised payment establishment, which is not a bank. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 [OFT Tunisie, a subsidiary of Ooredoo, received definitive authorisation](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2026/03/16/oft-tunisie-obtient-lautorisation-definitive-pour-exercer-comme-etablissement-de-paiement/>) as one. On 25 September 2026 the central bank issued [Circular n° 2026-10 on payment establishments](<https://www.tunisienumerique.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/circulaire-25-septrembre.pdf>), replacing a 2018 circular, which lets them open client payment accounts and issue electronic payment instruments. No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Tanzania's [National Payment Systems Act, 2015](<https://bot.go.tz/Publications/Acts,%20Regulations,%20Circulars,%20Guidelines/Acts/en/2020030902433783.pdf>) was assented to on 25 April 2015 and gazetted on 22 May 2015. It puts payment systems, payment instruments and electronic money under Bank of Tanzania licensing. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no regulation made under the Act is named. No source has been found that says companies other than banks are licensed under it, or names one licensed. Operating would need a source that says so, or names one licensed.

Uganda's law is the [National Payment Systems Act, 2020](<https://kikubolane.com/2026/09/15/ugandas-central-bank-to-probe-claims-mobile-money-users-are-paying-off-strangers-loans/>). Bank of Uganda officials told a parliamentary committee on 14 September 2026 that the wallet providers the bank licenses and supervises are MTN and Airtel, mobile money operators that are not banks. In the last twelve months, [NALA, a Tanzanian firm, announced payment service provider and payment system operator licences from the Bank of Uganda in December 2025](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/brief/brief-simple/tanzanian-fintech-nala-receives-uganda-payment-service-system-licenses>), and [Payaza a payment system operator licence in February 2026](<https://techcabal.com/2026/02/11/payaza-expands-east-african-footprint-with-uganda-license/>). No rule has been found that requires providers to connect to each other. Mature would need such a rule.

South Africa's [National Payment System Act of 1998](<https://facephi.com/observatory/en/national-payment-system-south-africa-psp-licences/>) gives the Reserve Bank responsibility for clearing and settlement. [The Reserve Bank has designated non-banks as clearing system participants under it](<https://www.resbank.co.za/en/home/what-we-do/payments-and-settlements/regulation>), among them Yoco Technologies in 2021 and Payfast in 2024. In the last twelve months it [published a draft framework in May 2026](<https://techcabal.com/2026/10/26/south-africa-fintech-payment-network/>) that would let approved non-banks issue e-money. [On 1 September 2026 the governor said a National Payment System Bill](<https://techcentral.co.za/national-payment-system-bill-sarb-fintech/285597/>) would soon go out for comment. No rule has been found that requires mobile money providers and banks to connect to each other or to a switch. Mature would need such a rule.

Zambia's [National Payment Systems Act](<https://www.boz.zm/national-payment-systems-act.htm>) was enacted by parliament on 12 April 2007 and empowers the Bank of Zambia to regulate payment mechanisms. Under it and the Bank of Zambia Act 2022 the bank [issued directives on e-money charges, binding from 2 August 2024](<https://regalert.today/document/directives-on-unwarranted-charges-and-fees-on-electronic-money-services-bca3f339-2d82-4256-967c-905e4917c5f1>), which bind e-money institutions, banks and financial institutions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found that says companies other than banks can be licensed under the Act, or names one licensed. Operating would need a source that says so, or names one licensed.

Zimbabwe's [National Payment Systems Act (Chapter 24:23)](<https://zimlii.org/akn/zw/act/2001/21/eng@2016-12-31>), Act 21 of 2001, commenced on 16 November 2001 and provides for the recognition, operation, regulation and supervision of payment and clearing systems. The text held is consolidated to 31 December 2016. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no regulation made under the Act or later amendment is named. No source has been found that says companies other than banks can be licensed under it, or names one licensed. Operating would need a source that says so, or names one licensed.
